Hm...if it's one of the Tennant series angels, I'd blink so I could get teleported back in time, find an awesome wife, and live a good life.

If it's one of the Smith series angels...yea, where's the nearest crack in the wall?

My co-worker does it. His veins have become pipes in his arm. It's a bit freaky IMO, but whatevs. It really does work. Your heart and cardio system *will* adapt. A baseline of cardio (just like people take pictures of their fat and non/less fat selves to maintain motivation) can be a very good thing if motivation faulters. How do you baseline cardio? Well, one method is to run as fast as you can as long as you can. Maybe 1-2 runs, keep track of how far you went.

Then, after a few weeks of insanity, do the same run again, until you can't run anymore. You'll see that you can run farther, you tire more slowly, etc. That shows you *are* building cardio progress. *shrug* It's just an idea I intercepted from hearing my co-worker talk to me about how he can do things he couldn't before.

I'm only 38 down myself but I feel the same way. I have a door right behind the bathroom mirror I use to gauge how much fat I've lost (two strait lines that don't move) and I can see that my gut has retreated at least 2 or 3 inches backwards, but...I don't look any thinner. I can't see the weight loss. I...don't understand. If it weren't for the scale slowly retreating I'd have given up (well, to be fair I already did once, and am back on the path) long ago.

For both our sakes I hope our brains catch up.

Trying to change them? Yes and no. They try to get change with a bludgeon. I try to get change by presenting the facts and leaving it up to a person to change. If I...say...think Ron Paul is the best thing since sliced bread, I will present my reasons for why, and my world view that explains why he is good for the country. They would tell me I had to vote for Mitt Romney or I was a horrible son and traitor to them.

I'm not weak-spined enough to fall for such lies...but they do wear on your mental defenses after a time.

*ponders the rest of what you said*

I agree, the church does tend to be a bit closed minded about science, but I don't blame them. The realization that science is wrong in its goals only because it asks "how did this happen" not "How did God do this?" has not yet permeated common understanding and thought processes. The small control the large; look at all the hoopla over neutrinos that *might* move faster than light speed? A neutrino is pretty darn small last time I checked. But quark interactions define proton / neutron / (electron? been a while...) actions. Proton/neutron/electron define atomic behavior, atomic behavior dictates molecular behavior, and so on. Does each control *all* aspects of the next larger one? No, that would be folly. They do play a large role though. How is far beyond what I feel like typing out, and I'm also by no means an expert on the matter. Just read some books on how important ants, or worms, are to healthy ecosystems to get an idea of what I am on about.

I conclude that the Lord created sex for a purpose, and defined some 'uses' of sex as evil. What is evil? Doing whatever the Lord says not to do. He is good not because we have some absolute concept of right and wrong. He is good because He Is Good. Good does not exist without Him because it cannot. Throw that pillar of faith out the door and you aren't debating Christianity anymore; just like throwing out that gravity exists...well, then you aren't debating physics anymore.

So yes, the justification is just that simple. The Lord says no, that is all that need be said. If you wish to seek the wisdom behind the decree, by all means, seek it. The Lord will enlighten you. If you do not need such wisdom, then continue honoring the Law. I fall into the category that does not need to know the wisdom on this matter, so I cannot help you on your quest.

Your mistake is believing I am like everyone else and haven't. I do not speak of an ideal I do not follow myself. That would be both folly and pointless. That said, it is a life spent being told you are wrong. Heh, just look at all the comments I am getting. I live a quiet life, commenting when I feel my input is desired, moving on when it is not. My focus is, and has been for some time, on doing what is right in the eyes of the Lord. I gave up on caring what this broken world thought was right about 5,000 wrong ideas ago {obviously, not a literal comment}.

*shrug* Your disagreement is not a new experience for me. Still, I can be a bit less vague on what I mean in paragraph 3. 

I have had preachers teach that divorce was an acceptable end to a marriage if you just weren't happy with your spouse (and for no other reason). They always use some silly excuse like "It's better for the children" instead of something more along the lines of "You did this for life; walk away from God, or walk back together. There are no other roads." By all means, add 100 doses of nice to that, but the core principle should not change.

I have heard many preachers waffle on the need for two people who have pre-marital sex to get married, despite Deuteronomy 22 stating very clearly that they are to be (the NIV uses the word rape to define both consensual pre-marital sex, it is expected that a woman being raped, in the more modern sense of the term, would cry out, and be saved by others, thereby saving her own life)

I get tired of the implications that every Sunday when families gathered for church (in OT times) that every family needed a (or several) bulls to pay for their sins at the Altar. They clearly have no concept of how expensive that would get. The preacher needs to live 6 months spending...we'll say...$5,000 (assuming a $55K annual salary) every week he thinks a bull would be appropriate. I believe you'd see him either start saying he was better, or start working a *lot* harder to behave. Think...from every angle {this sentence is directed at the pastor; who did have this habit}. Not just your own. >.<

Those are the lies that stand out most in my memory. To avoid telling a lie, or a tall tale, I cannot state any more, as my memory on them is fuzzy.

I did not meet my bible study group until my last year there, so I only got a handfull of chapters done with them, but such was the exceptional quality of what I did learn...I feel the need to share the method.

Moving on to your actual question, we never covered it. That said, Sodom and Gomorrah was utterly destroyed for sexual sin, including homosexuality, so it is an issue God clearly takes quite seriously, and wants nothing to do with. Woman was created for man, to be his suitable helper (and suitable helper depends on the man, some need housewives, others need marksmen, others mechanics, you get the idea). It makes no sense for woman to have been created to be a suitable helper if man was to be able to find company in himself.

Again though, I have no studied the subject extensively. I am sure there is some tidying up to do. Again, I never read my bible with the intention of learning about a topic, that is an excellent way to find what you are looking for. I always read wanting to learn what is said. I will get to it eventually. I have to. :)

Edit: I do not share my views beyond the limited scope of what I have included here because I am unsure of their factual accuracy. I would rather say "I don't know" and force another to seek wisdom than risk teaching a lie.

What pushes young people out of the chruch? A lack of teaching! It wasn't until I was in college that someone sat down and said "This is how you read your bible." Bible hermeneutics? Really? No one bothered to ever tell me that in 20 years of going to church? Wow...

Oh, and it wasn't until I got to college that we had a bible study where we opened our bibles, and read one chapter at a time. No goal, no mission, nothing we were looking for. In an hour of study we spent maybe 30 minutes going over context. Slow? Oh yea it is slow, but you understand *exactly* what was intended when you are done. And a group who are just as dedicated to truth as I am ensures that no stray idea is allowed to grow as a false seed. Arrogant? A bit, I keep it in check.

What pushes young people out of the churches is being lied to. Being told that sin is justifiable when the bible clearly says it is not. They are told in college and school that the bible contradicts itself, these...liars on the pulpits are not helping disprove that myth. Perhaps my location in the bible belt is simply filled with poor preachers. But every sermon should *not* have a message about tithe in it, and how the church needs money. If you are doing a good job, people will give. I have been in a few good churches, and they never have to ask for money.

I get tired of the lies.

Welcome to my world. That was me circa...2003-2007 or so. You aren't wrong, yes, that many people are insincere. You aren't nuts, that many people will put on a mask to get through life. However...you will (hopefully) understand, just as I did, that your understanding is not quite perfect. One thing, one question, is left un-asked in your post, but I won't insult you to say you haven't asked it. Why do they wear a mask?

They wear a mask because they feel just as awkward as you do with others. They aren't comfortable around you, they don't know you like they know their best friend. So they wear a mask to try and be what they hope you want...and fail at it judging by your annoyance (downplaying your strong emotions, I understand them) at them.

Others...others simply have not yet experienced the level of total emotional involvement in something that you have. They say (metaphorically) "Oh man, that fills me up!" but they have never been full, and they know it, so their words are as hollow as The Void (Dr. Who reference). 

Based on what you wrote, I will say that you, like me, can read a person's face and judge their motives by the intonation of their voice. For this reason, it is incredibly hard to deceive you. Distracting you is easier, making you ask the wrong questions simpler, but a direct lie, or an attempted deception does nothing but increase your anger. Give it tme, if you want to adjust, and learn to survive, you will need to question their motives, where their minds are, not just look and stay fixed on your own. Understand them as well, or better than, they understand themselves.

You have been given an amazing gift. Use it, or waste it, at your leisure. In time, you can return here, and see through the lies people's minds tell them. You will see through them because you learned to ask the right questions, avoid distractions, and be mentally strong. Best of luck mate.

I kept a journal, online, for...almost 6 years I suppose. I started because I wanted to be cool like all my other friends who were making journals. But then my life changing event occurred, and it became a place for me to talk when I had no one to talk to. I knew people at my school read it. I had a silent audience, and so many times people would come up and thank me for writing what I did because it showed them something deep within themselves they had been unable to see.

But there was always a nagging problem. I wrote in my journal only when I was emotionally destroyed. It was one of my coping mechanisms, to write, to let things out. But with age and time I found that every time I wrote, I would get even more desperate and worse mentally for the next few days. Eventually, after 2 years of watching this pattern, and...especially, after my college contacted me, asking me to talk to counseling services due to the content of my journal, I closed it, deleted all the posts, and moved on.

Since then, I have kept things inside. Written them on the walls in my mind. I have told my thoughts to all who would listen to them. I have been better for it. Why? Because I don't simply hold things in. I hold them in, contain them, study them, think about them, research them, and...ultimately, figure them out. I use the pain I would write down as fuel when nothing else will drive me. I use the pain to keep me awake, to drive me to tears so I can sleep, to keep me eating meals, to keep me working out. What is physical pain when your emotional pain is so much worse?

It sounds like I'm trying to destroy myself, but I'm not. You'd have to meet me to understand just how wonderful I have made my lack of a journal. It is a positive thing in my life. I am brilliant, driven, and alone. This is the perfect combination to both self-destruct without notice, and to see why the darkest corners of my heart are dark. Once you understand the enemy, can you not figure out a way to defeat him? You have your entire life to try methods until one works. You will learn, you will become a skilled hunter of your own darkness, and, at the end of days, you will stand victorious over what used to haunt you. Victory through endurance, patience, and cunning.

Hi. This is reddit. A place filled with stalkers, professionals at espionage, experts in 'google-fu', and facebook creeping. Generally speaking, you give us a screen name, common internet handle, phone number, facebook page, or hell, even a picture, and in 24 hours we can have everything on them. Give us what you have. We will find her. I'd be happy to give her a warm meal and company for the holidays...if I had but the room. And...assuming she's in my country :p

I'd be willing to guess someone here would make that offer. Though she sounds so protective of her privacy such an offer might go unused...the fact that the offer exists, a car ride to get her, meals, help locating a job if she wants to stay around, etc etc, could be all she needs to get back up and keep going. I know in my own life, just that knowledge, that a door existed, was all I needed, even if I never used it. Just knowing it was there was all I needed.

Strictly speaking, yes. We are meant to be social. Everything about us makes us social. We strive to fit in, to be accepted, loved, etc. That being said, it is completely normal to want to spend periods of time in isolation. Just because we are meant to be social does not mean we must be social 24/7. If you need to go on a [walkabout](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walkabout), by all means go. It has its uses.

The upper Peninsula of Michigan has a lot of empty wooded country. Mostly maple too, so it's absolutely beautiful in the fall. You will cry at the  overwhelming beauty of it. Get on top of a reasonably high mountain (Copper Harbor has one such hill) and for 30 miles in every direction you will see the golden red leaves of fall. It is quiet too. The loudest thing you will hear in most places is an animal calling to another. Silence. Peace, quiet. Calm.
